ko.text: The public launch hits its traction target

name: Food Rescue Startup
scope: Mobile app, partner business acquisition, marketing, user research and the business model. Nobody knows yet what exactly will work.
approachText: High uncertainty: nobody knows what users want or which business model will work. The whole project is best managed in an agile way: short iterations, testing hypotheses and data-driven decisions. A detailed plan would rest on untested assumptions.
intro: You're co-founding a startup that connects restaurants and shops with leftover food to people nearby. The money lasts 12 weeks – by then you must prove people actually want the app.

terms.poGood: co-founder in charge of the product

workstreams.name: Mobile app (MVP)
workstreams.why: Only users will show what the app should do. Small releases, fast feedback, adjustments.

workstreams.name: User research
workstreams.why: Research runs continuously and its questions change with whatever the team just learned.

workstreams.name: Partner business acquisition
workstreams.why: Which pitch wins businesses over can only be found by trying – a pilot with a few, then adjust.

workstreams.name: Marketing and growth
workstreams.why: Channels and messages are tested in short experiments, and money goes where it works.

workstreams.name: Business model and pricing
workstreams.why: Careful, even though it sounds like planning: nobody knows upfront how much people and businesses will pay. It's tested by experiments.

workstreams.name: Brand and design
workstreams.why: Design is tuned with users; the first version can be simple and improve over time.

workstreams.name: Metrics and analytics
workstreams.why: What to measure gets clearer as the team learns its product and market.

workstreams.name: Investor talks
workstreams.why: The pitch is tuned to investor reactions and fresh traction data – iterative work.

discoveries.name: Alerts for food nearby
discoveries.why: After reservations go live, users write: "Let me know when something shows up nearby!"

discoveries.name: Sharing savings on social media
discoveries.why: Users screenshot the savings counter and share it. They want to do it right from the app.

milestones.name: First users
milestones.okText: The first users are using the app and coming back.
milestones.lateText: The app isn't giving users enough value yet.

milestones.name: Demo Day
milestones.okText: At demo day you can show growing numbers.
milestones.lateText: At demo day there are no numbers that would convince investors.

milestones.name: Public launch
milestones.okText: The app has traction: people use it and recommend it!
milestones.lateText: The app is out, but traction is weak.

gate.title: Demo day: more money?
gate.text: Investors are deciding whether the startup gets money for another 6 months. What will you show them?
gate.lesson: In an agile project the best basis for a decision is a working product and data on what the team learned – failures included.

choices.text: A live product, traction metrics and what we learned (including what didn't work)
choices.feedback: Investors were impressed by how fast the team learns. Funding for the next period is secured.

choices.text: Slides with a big vision and market estimates, no data
choices.feedback: "Nice vision. So how many people use it today?" Silence.

choices.text: Postpone the demo until everything is done
choices.feedback: Investors postponed their decision and the money is running thin.

events.title: Users use it differently
events.text: Data shows people open the app mostly on Friday afternoons – for bakery goods, not restaurants.
events.lesson: Data on user behavior beats the original vision. Findings get validated and reflected in the backlog.

choices.text: Validate it with user interviews and update the backlog
choices.feedback: Interviews confirmed it. Friday bakery deals were added to the backlog.

choices.text: Stick to the original vision: restaurants
choices.feedback: Users keep coming for bread – the app just doesn't support it in any way.

choices.text: Rebuild everything around bakeries right now
choices.feedback: Maybe the right direction, but unvalidated and with a derailed sprint.

events.title: Big competition
events.text: A big delivery company announced a similar feature in its app.
events.lesson: Against big players a startup wins by learning faster and staying focused, not by copying.

choices.text: Focus on what makes us different (local businesses, community) and test it
choices.feedback: Local businesses love that the startup knows them personally. The test confirmed interest.

choices.text: Copy all their features
choices.feedback: The team is chasing a giant at its own game. No chance.

choices.text: Ignore it
choices.feedback: Nothing changed – but the team doesn't know how to stand out.

events.title: Companies are calling
events.text: Three companies reached out wanting to offer leftover cafeteria food to their employees through the app. It's a whole different segment.
events.lesson: A pivot is a strategy change based on validated learning – not a panic move, nor stubborn clinging to the original vision.

choices.text: Test the hypothesis with a cheap experiment (landing page + 5 interviews), then decide
choices.feedback: The experiment showed strong interest. The value of "Packages for corporate cafeterias" is now validated.

choices.text: Pivot to companies right away and ditch the rest
choices.feedback: Bold, but unvalidated. The team also threw away ideas in progress.

choices.text: Refuse – that's not our vision
choices.feedback: The opportunity went elsewhere.

events.title: Running out of money
events.text: The money will barely last the rest of the planned period. The investor wants to see that the product makes sense.
events.lesson: With limited resources, focus on the metric that shows real value and cut everything that doesn't lead to it.

choices.text: Focus on repeat reservations and cut the "Could" features
choices.feedback: The team only builds what drives repeat use. The money will last.

choices.text: Spend the rest on ads to get the numbers up
choices.feedback: Downloads spiked, but people don't come back. And the money is gone.

choices.text: Freeze development and save
choices.feedback: The money lasts longer, but the product isn't moving.

events.title: Friday night outage
events.text: The app crashed on Friday evening – right at peak traffic.
events.lesson: An incident is a chance to improve the process. Look for the cause in the system, not for someone to blame.

choices.text: Fix it, then a blameless retrospective + monitoring and tests in the Definition of Done
choices.feedback: Cause found; monitoring now raises the alarm before users notice.

choices.text: Find out who broke it
choices.feedback: The team is scared and bugs start getting swept under the rug.

choices.text: Pay for beefier servers and leave it at that
choices.feedback: It helped, but the real cause remained.

events.title: Businesses don't want another tablet
events.text: Partner restaurants refuse to install the business app. "Just text us, we'll reply."
events.lesson: The simplest solution that works for users is often the best MVP.

choices.text: Build the simplest SMS version and test it with three businesses
choices.feedback: The businesses love it. Two days brought more new offers than the whole past month.

choices.text: Insist on the business app
choices.feedback: Two businesses ended the partnership.

choices.text: Hire salespeople to win them over
choices.feedback: They won over a few businesses, but the expensive way.
